description: Floyd-Warshall computes the shortest-path distance between every pair of vertices in `O(n³)` time. Round `k` lets every path pass through vertex `k`: `D[i][j] ← min(D[i][j], D[i][k] + D[k][j])`. For a consistent simple temporal network (STN), these distances give the *minimal network*: each pair of time points gets the tightest interval `[−D[j][i], D[i][j]]`, and every value in that interval occurs in some valid schedule. A negative entry on the diagonal shows a negative cycle, so the network is inconsistent. `temporal-control` stops at the first negative diagonal entry, which keeps the distances exact.

papers.authors: Rina Dechter, Itay Meiri, Judea Pearl
papers.title: Temporal constraint networks
